resources.string: Unlock the phone or tap Stop
Not paired. Open Tether to pair.

On the iPhone, open the Camera, point it at this code and tap Open in Cellular (or in Cellular: Link › Pair with Android phone). Allow Bluetooth when the iPhone asks. The code works once and expires in 5 minutes.
Do these steps once, top to bottom. Each one says what to do; a step is done when it turns green.
Tap Grant and allow everything Tether asks for: phone, SMS, contacts, call log, nearby devices (Bluetooth) and notifications. Tether passes them on to your iPhone; nothing leaves your devices.
Tap Set and choose Tether as the default phone app, so calls can be answered and made from the iPhone.
Tap Set and allow unrestricted battery use, so Android does not stop Tether while the phone sits in a bag.

One time only, needs Wi-Fi. Turn on Developer options (Settings › About phone › Software information: tap Build number 7 times). Tap Pair: Tether opens Developer options and posts a notification. Turn on Wireless debugging, tap Pair device with pairing code, then type the 6-digit code into Tether\'s notification. This lets Tether carry call audio.
Next: tap Pair iPhone below and scan the code with the iPhone.
iPhone app 1.1 or older? Show the old code
Code for Cellular 1.1: in Cellular open Link › Pair with Android phone and scan it there (the Camera app cannot open this one).
TCP debugging (Android 8 to 10, or no Wi-Fi)

Connect this phone to a computer with USB once, run: adb tcpip 5555, and accept the key prompt on the phone (Always allow). Tether then connects to 127.0.0.1:5555 itself. Repeat the adb tcpip command after every restart of the phone. Turn it off again with: adb usb. While it is on, the phone accepts adb connections on every network it is on, protected only by that key approval.
Could not connect to adb on port %1$d. Run adb tcpip %1$d from a computer and accept the key prompt.
Open Developer options › Wireless debugging › Pair device with pairing code, then type the 6-digit code here.
Paired with Wireless debugging. Starting the audio helper…
Forget %1$s? It will need to be paired again.
Call audio needs Android 11 or later. On this phone, calls are still answered, placed and ended from the iPhone, but their audio stays on this phone.
Call audio on Android 11 and 12 uses the phone\'s call recorder path and works only if this phone allows it. Run the self-test during a call to check.

This phone\'s software gave Tether no call audio in a call (the call sounded like silence to it), so calls are not bridged here: they are still answered, placed and ended from the iPhone, but you hear and speak on this phone. A system update, or a self-test during a call that hears the call, turns call audio back on. If calls on the phone itself have no sound either, restart the phone once.
Call audio needs Android 13 or later. On this phone, calls are still answered, placed and ended from the iPhone, but their audio stays on this phone.
On: Tether checks during each call that your voice still reaches the other side and turns the mute off if it does not.
On, but not used on this phone: here Android\'s microphone mute also silences your voice for the other side, so the phone\'s microphone stays on during calls.
On, but not used on this phone: muting the microphone silenced your voice for the other side. Switch it off and on to try again.
This phone\'s microphone during bridged calls

Tether takes this phone\'s own microphone and earpiece out of the call: with Android\'s redirect audio mode where this phone handles it, else with the phone maker\'s own microphone switch. It checks that both directions still work and remembers what this phone allows.
Android\'s redirect mode does not work on this phone: Tether mutes this phone\'s microphone with the maker\'s own switch instead, which keeps your voice in the call.
This phone does not allow it (or needs Android 13): its microphone stays on during calls, so keep it in a bag or pocket. Choose this again to try anew.
This phone\'s microphone stays in the call: the other side may hear your voice twice, and the room around this phone.
was silenced by the redirect mode; it is no longer used on this phone
was silenced by the microphone mute; the mute is now off on this phone
nothing mutes it on this phone
not checked (this phone cannot show it)
Type the 6-digit code shown under Pair device with pairing code.
Wireless debugging needs Wi-Fi. Connect to a Wi-Fi network, open Pair device with pairing code again and enter the new code.
The pairing window was not found. Keep Pair device with pairing code open on screen (pull this notification down over it, or use split screen) and enter the code while it is shown.
The code was wrong or has expired. Open Pair device with pairing code again and enter the new 6-digit code.
Paired, but could not connect yet (%1$s). Tether tries again while Wireless debugging is on.

One file with what is needed to find a problem with setup, pairing, the link, calls, call audio, texts, contacts or tethering. Phone numbers, names, message text, e-mail, addresses and keys are left out. Attach it to your issue on GitHub.
Preparing the report… This can take up to half a minute.
The report is ready (%1$d KB). Phone numbers, names, message text, e-mail, addresses and keys are removed; please look through it before you post it.
The report could not be made: %1$s
Copied, shortened to %1$d KB for the clipboard. Share sends the whole file.
